about: Ties a client timeline dummy to the timeline that drives it: Actor (the actor's id in the timeline), Timeline (the running timeline's id), Slot, IsListener, IsAdditional. While Timeline names a running timeline, that timeline's transform track writes the dummy's Transform every frame; with the null guid there the dummy is left alone and keeps its animation.

in the main menu level SYS_Menuscreen_Act3_B a Transform written to an adventurer dummy of MM_Accept_Temple is back at the timeline's value on the next read, also when written on every tick; after Timeline is set to the null guid the written Transform stays, and with Visual:SetWorldTranslate the figure is drawn at the new place

questions.ask: which function of the timeline systems (ecl::TimelineTransformFlushSystem is a candidate by name) reads Timeline and writes the Transform; a probe on its update while a dummy is detached would show it

survey.names: Every name here is Script Extender's author's (his headers), not the game's own: they are kept because they are what the extender's Lua answers to and what bg3_verify compares, and every field carries the rung `extender` - the extender's name for the field at that offset, which nobody has checked against the game's code. A name is raised from `extender` only with evidence from the code, by `gatekit names set`.
